title: Honorary doctorate from Princeton
summary: Carter was stunned to receive an honorary Doctorate of Humanities, to great applause.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Then, at the end of that year, I think you were somewhat, at the end of that academic year, you perhaps were somewhat surprised by another offer from Princeton.
Indeed. That was the one that ... oh, well, I don't know what to say about that. You know, it's ...
The truth. That's what we want.

Well, that was when I was informed that I was to receive the Honorary Doctorate of the Humanities, and I didn't know what I had done to deserve it, you know. I said, "Well, ..." and I was kind of stunned, and very, very happily. I haven't really gotten over it yet! I'm still trying to get used to it.

Well, that was one of the best honorary degrees that I think the university had given out for a very, very long time -- if not forever, and I remember myself, at the time, that each person that receives an honorary degree got a certain amount of applause from the audience, but I think that the applause that you got was much greater than all the others put together, and it was quite clear that among the students, at least, that granting you the degree was a much more popular affair than granting it to anybody else who had been there.

So that was a great thing for Princeton, as well as for you.

We continue down to the very, very immediate present.

I want to go back to the ending of this long period without recording an album. The last albums, we mentioned earlier, were until the mid-sixties; I think '66 was the date of the additions to Further Definitions.
